svg.title: Compensating Transaction
svg.desc: Compensating Transaction. Undo the completed steps of a multi-step operation that failed part-way. Step 1, Can't be rolled back: Flight and hotel are booked in their own systems; the car fails. No transaction spans all three. Step 2, Undo by compensating: Cancel the hotel, then the flight: new operations, not a restore. The airline keeps a $40 fee. Step 3, Compensations fail too: The hotel's cancel times out. Retrying is safe (same key); after 3 attempts a person takes over. Step 4, Design for cheap undo: Hold first, pay last: the car fails, so nothing is confirmed and the holds lapse by themselves.

g.text: Flight and hotel are booked in their own systems; the car fails. No transaction spans all three.
Cancel the hotel, then the flight: new operations, not a restore. The airline keeps a $40 fee.
The hotel's cancel times out. Retrying is safe (same key); after 3 attempts a person takes over.
Hold first, pay last: the car fails, so nothing is confirmed and the holds lapse by themselves.
book flight → book hotel → book car
hold seat → hold room → hold car →
each entry is saved before the next step runs
✕ no transaction spans the three systems: nothing to roll back
saved before each next step, so a new worker knows what is left
each retry reuses one key: cancelling twice = one cancellation
each hold expires on its own unless the workflow confirms it
a failure just means not confirming: the holds lapse by themselves
